// globals.mjs.txt — THE ES GLOBALS, ONE SITE PER CLAIM.
//
// WHY A NEW FIXTURE RATHER THAN A LINE IN alpha.mjs. Measured 2026-09-09 over
// the five files of test/fixtures/js-call: the corpus contains `String(n)`,
// `new Error(...)`, `new Promise(...)` and `Symbol.iterator`, and NOT ONE call
// to a static of an ES global — no `JSON.parse`, no `Object.entries`, no
// `Math.max`, no `Promise.all`. So the static surface had no site at all and
// every claim about it would have been vacuous. This file supplies the sites.
//
// IT IS `.txt` AND NOT `.mjs` ON PURPOSE. test/js-modules.test.ts imports every
// `.mjs` in test/fixtures/js-call with node and compares default exports
// set-for-set; a sixth module there is another branch's oracle changing under
// it. The price is stated rather than hidden: nothing RUNS this file, so its
// claims are checked against TypeScript's declarations and not against V8.
//
// EVERY SITE BELOW EARNS ITS PLACE BY BEING THE ONLY ONE OF ITS KIND. The four
// declaration forms, the three surfaces, the two shapes of a static, both
// residues, and the one negative control that makes the free-name test
// load-bearing.

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1. A NAMESPACE OBJECT — `declare var JSON: JSON`. Not new-able, no prototype
//    surface, and its two members are the whole of it. es5.
export function roundTrip(text) {
  return JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(text));
}

// 2. STATICS OF A CONSTRUCTOR BINDING, AT THREE DIFFERENT RELEASES, which is
//    what makes the era gate a comparison rather than a slope: `keys` is es5,
//    `entries` es2017 and `hasOwn` es2022, all three off the same global.
export function describe(bag) {
  return Object.keys(bag).length + Object.entries(bag).length
       + (Object.hasOwn(bag, 'lid') ? 1 : 0);
}

// 3. es2020 AND es2021 OFF ANOTHER CONSTRUCTOR, so the gate discriminates two
//    globals rather than two members of one.
export function settleAll(work) {
  return Promise.allSettled(work).then((r) => Promise.any(r));
}

// 4. CALLABLE AND DATA ON ONE GLOBAL. `Math.max` is a MethodSignature in
//    TypeScript's declaration and `Math.PI` is a PropertySignature, and that is
//    the whole of the difference the model reads.
export function widest(a, b) {
  return Math.max(a, b) * Math.PI;
}

// 5. THE SAME SPLIT WHERE IT MATTERS MOST. `Symbol.for` is a call and
//    `Symbol.iterator` is a KEY — a well-known symbol exists to be written as a
//    computed property name, and nothing about the spelling says so.
export const tagged = {
  [Symbol.iterator]() { return { next: () => ({ done: true }) }; },
  stamp: Symbol.for('rofl.globals'),
};

// 6. THE NAMESPACE-BLOCK FORM — `declare namespace Reflect`. TypeScript declares
//    no variable for it at all, so a walk that only reads `declare var` finds
//    `Math` and misses this. es2015.
export function ownedKeys(target) {
  return Reflect.ownKeys(target);
}

// 7. A CONSTRUCTOR BINDING CONSTRUCTED, whose INSTANCE surface this model does
//    not carry: there is no `kind_prototype` row for a `new_expression`, so
//    `holder.set` is not a `lib_member` question and the missing
//    `lib_global_prototype("Map", ...)` row is where that shows.
export function fresh(k, v) {
  const holder = new Map();
  holder.set(k, v);
  return holder;
}

// 8. A STATIC THE ECMASCRIPT SURFACE DOES NOT CARRY. `Error.captureStackTrace`
//    is V8's, not the language's — TypeScript declares it in @types/node and
//    nowhere in lib.es*.d.ts — so this is the positive control for the residue
//    audit, which would otherwise be empty and unfalsifiable.
export function whereFrom(holder) {
  Error.captureStackTrace(holder, whereFrom);
  return holder;
}

// 9. A FREE GLOBAL THE ECMASCRIPT SURFACE DOES NOT KNOW AT ALL. `console` is
//    the runtime's and `globalThis` is a compiler intrinsic no lib.es*.d.ts
//    declares. Both land in `global_unattributed[audit]`, which is the relation
//    the runtime half of this question joins against.
export function announce(n) {
  console.log(n);
  return globalThis.crypto;
}

// 10. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL, AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THE FREE-NAME TEST MEAN
//     ANYTHING. `Set` here is a local binding that shadows the global of the
//     same name; `Set.of` is a call on a value in this program and must NOT be
//     attributed to the standard library. Without this line, `not
//     declares_name` could be deleted and every assertion in the file would
//     still pass.
export function shadowed(rows) {
  const Set = { of: (xs) => xs.length };
  return Set.of(rows);
}

// 11. A FORM THAT IS NOT CONSTRUCTIBLE, CONSTRUCTED. `new Math()` is a
//     TypeError at runtime and the model can now say why: `Math` is a
//     `namespace_object` and there is no constructor interface behind it. The
//     function is never called; the SITE is the point.
export function neverRun() {
  return new Math();
}

// 12. A CONSTRUCTOR BINDING CALLED AS A FUNCTION AND NOT CONSTRUCTED, which is
//     a third thing to do with a binding and needs its own relation: `new
//     BigInt(n)` is a TypeError and `BigInt(n)` is the whole point of it. It is
//     also es2020, so the BINDING gate has something to say about four
//     environments rather than only about es5.
export function asBig(n) {
  return BigInt(n);
}

// 13. THE CEILING, AS A LINE RATHER THAN AS A SENTENCE. `Infinity` is a
//     `plain_value` global and this reference is neither the object of a member
//     expression nor a callee, so `global_ref_position` cannot see it. The
//     model is silent here, and test/js-globals.test.ts asserts the silence by
//     name so that it is a stated limit rather than an unnoticed one.
export function ceiling(n) {
  return n > 0 ? n : Infinity;
}
